label: Primary construction aggregates
source_name: Mineral Products Association — Profile of the UK Mineral Products Industry 2025
source_record: 2024 GB primary aggregate supply: 109.3 Mt crushed rock + 50.0 Mt sand/gravel
methodology_note: Primary aggregate supply figure. It is not the total mass of all UK virgin materials.

label: Primary aggregates entering material supply
methodology_note: Stage-transfer estimate: the 159.3 Mt primary aggregate supply is carried from Extraction to Material Processing/Supply for diagrammatic continuity. This does not imply every tonne undergoes a distinct industrial processing step.
scope_note: Designer stage mapping of a source-supported quantity.

label: Recycled & secondary aggregates
source_record: 74.7 Mt recycled and secondary aggregates used in 2024
methodology_note: A real recovered-material input. This is a useful large-scale return loop.
scope_note: Recycled/secondary aggregates accounted for just under a third of total GB aggregate supply.

label: Aggregate supply to construction/fabrication
methodology_note: Derived as 159.3 Mt primary + 74.7 Mt recycled/secondary = 234.0 Mt total aggregate supply.
scope_note: Do not add cement or concrete constituent streams to this as though they are independent mass; some streams overlap conceptually.

label: Aggregates incorporated into construction
methodology_note: First-order design estimate carrying the 234.0 Mt aggregate supply into construction/use. It assumes the annual aggregate supply is substantially incorporated into built works; it is not a measured stock-addition figure.
scope_note: Use as a broad material-throughput picture, not a strict national material balance.

label: Iron ore-equivalent upstream input
source_name: World Steel / UK steel evidence + MIT global Sankey relationship
methodology_note: Estimate = UK crude steel production 4.0 Mt × (MIT global iron ore 2500 / downstream steel 1875) = 5.333 Mt iron-ore equivalent. This is not reported UK ore consumption and includes upstream extraction outside the UK.
scope_note: Used to make upstream material intensity visible. UK metal ore extraction itself is negligible relative to use.

label: Iron ore-equivalent to steel processing
source_name: World Steel / UK steel evidence + MIT global Sankey relationship
methodology_note: Carries the same 5.333 Mt upstream equivalent into the processing stage; not a measured UK import flow.

label: Crude steel produced
source_record: UK steel production in 2024 approximately 4 Mt
methodology_note: Domestic crude steel output. Finished steel demand is higher because the UK is a net importer.

label: Finished steel demand
source_record: Historical finished steel demand 2024 = 8.55 Mtpa
methodology_note: Demand includes imported steel, so it intentionally exceeds UK crude-steel production.

label: Steel scrap arising
source_name: UK Steel Strategy / Primary Steelmaking Review
source_record: UK produces around 10–11 Mt steel scrap annually
methodology_note: Midpoint estimate of reported 10–11 Mt annual scrap generation = 10.5 Mt. Scrap arises from products, vehicles, buildings and infrastructure placed into use in earlier years, so it need not equal current-year steel demand.

label: Steel scrap used domestically
source_record: Around 2.2 Mt steel scrap used domestically

label: Steel scrap surplus / exported
source_name: UK Steel Strategy / Primary Steelmaking Review
methodology_note: Derived midpoint remainder: 10.5 Mt estimated scrap generation − 2.2 Mt domestic use = 8.3 Mt. Government review states the remainder is largely exported; label remains 'surplus/export' rather than claiming every tonne is exported.

label: Steel to construction / structures
source_name: UK Steel Strategy Demand Assessment + MIT global Sankey allocation
methodology_note: Estimate = UK 2024 finished steel demand 8.55 Mt × MIT global downstream share 0.5200 = 4.446 Mt. This is an indicative design allocation, not a measured UK sector split.

label: Estimated energy for UK steelmaking
methodology_note: Estimate = 4.0 Mt UK crude steel × 20.95 GJ/t global average energy intensity = 83.8 PJ = 2.002 Mtoe. Actual UK route mix may differ substantially.

label: Estimated steelmaking CO2
methodology_note: Estimate = 4.0 Mt crude steel × 1.92 tCO2/t global average = 7.680 MtCO2. Do not add to an overview manufacturing-emissions estimate if that estimate already includes steel.

label: UK-grown roundwood for material uses
methodology_note: Derived as 10.4 Mt green roundwood deliveries − 2.4 Mt woodfuel = 8.0 Mt green tonnes for sawmills, panels, pulp/paper and other uses. 'Other' may include exports/fencing/shavings, so not all 8.0 Mt becomes manufactured products.

label: Roundwood entering material processing
methodology_note: Carries the 8.0 Mt green material-use roundwood estimate into processing.

label: Processed wood products — useful output estimate
source_name: Forest Research + MIT global Sankey wood-yield relationship
methodology_note: Estimate = 8.0 Mt green material-use roundwood × MIT useful-output ratio (460/560) = 6.571 Mt green-equivalent. Not a measured UK mass-yield.

label: Wood-processing residues estimate
source_name: Forest Research + MIT global Sankey wood-yield relationship
methodology_note: Estimate = 8.0 × MIT residue share (100/560) = 1.429 Mt green-equivalent. Some residues are useful co-products/energy feedstocks, so 'Waste/Losses' does not mean all is disposed.

label: Wood to construction estimate
source_name: Forest Research + MIT global Sankey allocation
methodology_note: Estimate = 8.0 × MIT construction share (110/560) = 1.571 Mt green-equivalent.

label: Wood to furniture / other products estimate

methodology_note: Estimate = 8.0 × MIT furniture/other share (350/560) = 5.000 Mt green-equivalent.

methodology_note: Energy demand is product/process dependent. Do not assign generic industry/domestic energy totals to this stage without a product-specific boundary.

label: Manufacturing GHG emissions
source_name: ONS Greenhouse gas emissions, UK: provisional estimates, 2024
source_record: Manufacturing emissions fell from 70 MtCO2e in 2023 to 65 MtCO2e in 2024

label: Estimated processing-stage GHG
source_name: ONS manufacturing GHG total + MIT global stage-energy proportions
methodology_note: Estimate allocates the 65 MtCO2e manufacturing total between Material Processing and Fabrication using MIT energy-use proportions for those two stages. Processing share 0.7047 → 45.803 MtCO2e. This is a design estimate and process emissions do not necessarily scale with energy use.

label: Estimated fabrication-stage GHG
source_name: ONS manufacturing GHG total + MIT global stage-energy proportions
methodology_note: Complementary estimate = 65 − 45.803 = 19.197 MtCO2e. Not an official UK stage statistic.

label: Extraction-stage GHG
source_name: ONS atmospheric emissions by industry and gas
methodology_note: Needs SIC mining/quarrying extraction mapping. Do not use total manufacturing GHG for extraction.

label: Use-stage operational GHG
methodology_note: Operational emissions vary radically by product: passive furniture/prosthetics versus vehicles, appliances and buildings. Quantify only in drill-down case studies.

label: End-of-use treatment GHG
methodology_note: Can later derive stage treatment emissions from waste quantities and route-specific conversion factors. Do not invent before treatment routes are mapped.

label: Domestic freight moved
source_name: DfT Transport Statistics Great Britain — Freight
source_record: 206 billion tonne-km domestic freight moved; 82% by road
methodology_note: All domestic freight, not just manufactured products. Show as a separate service overlay, never as a material mass backbone quantity.

label: HGV GHG emissions — freight proxy
source_name: DfT Greenhouse gas emissions from transport in 2024
source_record: HGVs emitted 18.4 MtCO2e in 2024
methodology_note: HGV emissions are a broad freight proxy; not all HGV activity distributes manufactured goods represented in this Sankey.

label: Transport energy for distribution
source_name: DESNZ Energy Consumption in the UK
methodology_note: Transport energy exists, but total transport energy includes passenger transport and aviation. Await freight-specific allocation rather than using all 54.0 Mtoe.

label: Land Disturbance
methodology_note: Potentially quantifiable for quarrying/mining, landfill and site-specific case studies. Needs consistent stage boundary.

methodology_note: Requires habitat-specific attribution; avoid converting generic extraction tonnage into habitat loss without spatial evidence.

label: Species Loss
methodology_note: Causal attribution to each manufacturing stage is complex; keep as annotation until a defensible indicator is selected.

label: Labour Exploitation
methodology_note: Important critical relationship but not commensurate with material/energy ribbons. Requires a defined social-risk metric.
